<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7844272c47fd4e83cae6f4770b878d70b5a37e13` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d8ebd74b77f92ef0115e0b8162eae7702f1f5e3` — the merge of head `c976f8c26c58c9a466906456f0b209f7abad376c` into base `7844272c47fd4e83cae6f4770b878d70b5a37e13`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1d8ebd74b77f92ef0115e0b8162eae7702f1f5e3 && git checkout 1d8ebd74b77f92ef0115e0b8162eae7702f1f5e3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7844272c47fd4e83cae6f4770b878d70b5a37e13 c976f8c26c58c9a466906456f0b209f7abad376c && git checkout -B drift-repro 7844272c47fd4e83cae6f4770b878d70b5a37e13 && git merge --no-ff c976f8c26c58c9a466906456f0b209f7abad376c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7844272c47fd4e83cae6f4770b878d70b5a37e13
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7844272c47fd4e83cae6f4770b878d70b5a37e13` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e7c804266c4d81c646a7286c0ad9506501e5849`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-only-local-password.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts (read only)

### ① Derived judgments

- The two door changes are exactly what the declaration says and nothing more: `runAdminSetUserPassword` returns `cloudManagedRefusal('setUserPassword')` before any source read when `isCloudManaged()` (after the 404 user check, so an unknown id still answers 404); `set-initial-password` refuses any caller with `session.user.id` under `isCloudManaged()`, anonymous falls through. Self-hosted paths are untouched (`isCloudManaged()` false ⇒ identical code), pinned by the two CONTROL cases. The removed `503` arm and the dropped `readUserSource` import are consistent.
- Tests drive the real seam (real `AuthManager`, mounted routes) and assert no credential is written or moved; ablations in the body match the hunks.
- **should-fix S1 — a third local-password door stays open on a managed environment.** `POST /request-password-reset` → `POST /reset-password` (and the phone twin) is not judged by `isCloudManaged()` anywhere: the before-hook only runs complexity/history there (`auth-manager-before-hook.ts` ~L244–280), the SSO-only judge in `sso-only-local-password.ts` applies only under SSO-only mode, and better-auth's reset mints the credential account on first set (`admin-import-users.ts` L35 relies on that). So on a hosted environment any user with a reachable email, an administrator included, can still be given a local password. Card #33203's goal is "nothing promises a password that hosted refuses", and the changeset, docs bullet, both refusal sentences ("no one holds a local password here") and the ADR note in #33248 all state the stronger rule. Either fold the reset doors in here (refuse `/reset-password` and `/phone-number/reset-password` with the managed 409 on `isCloudManaged()`, plus pins), or narrow every one of those sentences to the two doors and file one loose-ends card (p1, `lease:A1`) for the reset doors. Folding is preferred: it is the same rule and small.
- **should-fix S2 — "keeps" vs "sets".** The PR's own Unchanged list keeps a password a user already holds on a managed environment (cloud#4471 invalidates those). The refusal sentences say "no one holds a local password here", which is false for that user. Reword to what the code does: "no local password is set here for anyone, an administrator included". Same wording fix in #33248.
- nit N1: `auth-manager.ts` `signUpForcedOff` jsdoc still reads "Break-glass is untouched: neither case disables `emailAndPassword.enabled`". On a managed environment there is no break-glass now; reword the managed half.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with `fix(auth)!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is consistent with how this repo marks a runtime refusal under a deployment switch (no schema, no export moves). The `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker is correct: nothing stored to rewrite. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` is acceptable (no skill teaches these doors).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Security boundary: authentication doors on hosted environments; fail-closed direction. Lands only with ADR amendment #33248 (Tier H `docs/adr/**`), maintainer's word on both.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); implemented by area A1 session_016WV4d1NJYFGVi2FRztyBNo.
- CI at this head: Test Core / Build / Type Check / Lint still in progress when read (15:19Z), nothing red.
- UI follow-up already named in the body (Profile page still offers "set password" on managed).

### ④ Design judgment

The direction is right and matches ruling 10 of cloud#4465 as quoted on the card: hosted recovery is the cloud's, so a local break-glass credential is a route around the hosting IdP. Closing both doors for everyone (not by population) is the correct reading; the self-hosted D5.2 split is preserved. The design is incomplete only in S1: a rule stated as "no local password for anyone" must close every framework door that mints one, or be stated as narrower. With S1 and S2 fixed this is PASS.

Delta review of `7e7c8042..1ae420f9` (one commit), by the reviewer of record 6879603886.

### ① Derived judgments

- S1 fixed by folding. `globalBeforeHook` refuses `/reset-password`, `/phone-number/reset-password`, `/request-password-reset` and `/phone-number/request-password-reset` on `isCloudManaged()` with the managed `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. It runs ahead of the vendor handler, the per-number OTP send guard and the SSO-only reset judge, and before any record is read. So the answer is identical for every request and says nothing about any account (no enumeration signal, and nothing is spent). With the reset doors closed, no framework door mints a local credential on a managed environment. That makes the "sets no local password for anyone" rule true. Five wire pins; ablation reported all red.
- Declared consequence: on a managed environment a user who already holds a password can no longer reset it through these doors. That follows from the rule (the cloud refuses password sign-in, cloud#4477) and is in the changeset and docs.
- S2 fixed: every sentence now says "no local password is set (or reset) here for anyone". The docs say a password set before is not removed (cloud#4471).
- N1 fixed: the `signUpForcedOff` jsdoc now separates SSO-only (break-glass kept) from cloud-managed (none).
- The two door changes reviewed at 7e7c8042 are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch with `fix(auth)!` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, now naming six doors. The `adr-0087: not-required` marker is updated to six doors and still correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Authentication on hosted environments, fail-closed. Lands with ADR amendment #33248 (Tier H), maintainer's word on both.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area A1.
- CI at this head when read: 13 green, 16 running, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check.
- Follow-up already named in the body: the console's password UI on a managed environment (`domain:ui`).

### ④ Design judgment

With the reset doors folded in, the rule is enforced at every framework door that can create a local credential, as ruling 10 requires and as ADR-0135's amended note states. Refusing uniformly before any read is the right shape for a public door. Holds.

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff against `main` `12a0f09f` (the merge base, and the second merge's parent) is the declared change and nothing else: ten files, the eight in Scope plus the changeset and one docs bullet.
- `runAdminSetUserPassword`: on `isCloudManaged()` the door returns the managed `409` for every target, after the 404 for an unknown id and after `main`'s pending-person arm. The identity-source read and its `503` are gone from the managed arm, as declared. `readUserSource` stays imported because the pending arm uses it.
- Conflict resolution in `admin-user-endpoints.ts` (merge `3815aa85`): `main` had placed the pending arm above the managed arm; the resolution keeps that arm whole and replaces only the managed arm. Correct: both sides' rules hold, and nothing of `main`'s was dropped.
- `set-initial-password`: every caller with a session is refused on a managed environment; `isPlatformAdminUser` is still used by the SSO-only arm and elsewhere. A caller with no session falls through and is answered as before.
- `globalBeforeHook`: the four reset paths are refused on `isCloudManaged()` right after the one-account check and before the per-number send guard, the complexity and history checks, the SSO-only reset judge and the vendor handler. Nothing is read first, so the answer is the same for every request. The shape (`APIError('CONFLICT', { message, code })`) is the one the invite-member managed refusal already uses in this file.
- Other doors that could mint a credential on a managed environment, read on this head: sign-up is forced off (`signUpForcedOff`), `admin/create-user` and `admin/import-users` already refuse, `admin/add-sso-user` creates no password, the vendor email-OTP reset door is not mounted (`session-tombstone.ts` says so), and the only in-process `requestPasswordReset` caller is the refused import. So the sentence "sets no local password for anyone" holds at every framework door. `change-password` on a held credential is declared unchanged.
- Test commit `974fe1f3`: the two `pending-sso-users.test.ts` cases from `main` assumed the old managed arm. The platform-admin case now runs managed (managed sentence, the arm that answers first) and unmanaged (pending sentence); the env_native CONTROL runs unmanaged. Both changes follow the rule and keep the pending pins.
- S1: closed and S2: closed (record ID: 6879603886), still closed at this head.
- No must-fix, no should-fix.
- nit N1 — `set-user-password` judges the pending arm before the managed arm, `set-initial-password` the other way round. Both answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and write nothing; only the sentence differs. The docs bullet's "refuses every target" is true either way. Accepted as is.
- nit N2 — the PR body's "Lands with the ADR amendment #33248" and its Verification heads (`7e7c8042`, `1ae420f9`) are behind: #33248 is on `main` as `12a0f09f`, and the head moved. Prose only.

### ② Semver level

`Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no schema key, accepted value or authorable metadata moves; the six refusals are runtime answers under a deployment switch. `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch with `fix(auth)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` naming all six doors and the removed `503`, and a **BREAKING** paragraph in the changeset is consistent. `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: nothing stored to rewrite. The PR body and the changeset carry the same declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Authentication doors on hosted environments, fail-closed. The governing text is on `main`: ADR-0135 D5.2's note (#33248, `12a0f09f`) names the same six doors and the same kept-password clause as this diff.
- The PR is a draft; it is not ready to merge until the lane marks it ready.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); implemented by area A1.
- Check runs at this head: 38 success, 15 skipped, none red, none running.
- No new id materialisation or in-application join: the managed arm removes a read.
- Follow-up named in the body (`domain:ui`): the Profile page's "set password" card on a managed environment. The console's forgot-password entry was not read here; the same follow-up should cover it.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the published rule real rather than taking a declared capability away: ruling 10 of objectstack-ai/cloud#4465 and the ADR note on `main` say a hosted environment sets no local password for anyone, and before this change three framework doors still did. Refusing by deployment, not by population, is the right reading on a managed environment, and the self-hosted D5.2 split is untouched (the `isCloudManaged()` false path is the old code, pinned by CONTROL cases). Refusing the reset doors uniformly before any read is the right shape for a public door: no enumeration signal, nothing spent, and no link sent that the reset door would refuse. The code agrees with the contract it implements at each of the six doors.
